title: Winning the case does not make the money yours.
subtitle: A ruling in your favor cannot change the truth
then: Ibn 'Abbas said this is about someone who borrowed without proof, then {trap}denies the loan before the authorities{/trap} while knowing it is not his. The Prophet ﷺ said he was only human and might rule for the more persuasive party, but {trap}whoever takes another's right that way takes a piece of fire.{/trap}
now: The deposit your landlord cannot prove you owe back. The client who never put the agreement in writing. A clever argument might win. {idea}Allah already knows whose money it is.{/idea} Qatadah said the dispute will meet you again on the Day.
old: If no one can prove it, it is fair game.
new: A verdict can go my way and still leave me holding what is not mine.
try: Return or settle one thing you owe, even if the other person forgot.

title: Righteousness is not the back door. It is taqwa.
subtitle: New moons, old customs, and the real thing
then: People asked the Prophet ﷺ about the crescent moons, and the answer was practical: {idea}they mark time for people{/idea}, for worship and for Hajj. Al-Bara' said that before Islam people {trap}entered houses from the back{/trap} after assuming ihram, thinking it was piety. The verse says righteousness is taqwa.
now: A cousin swears you must do a special ritual nobody can trace. A post says one odd habit guarantees blessing. {trap}It looks devout.{/trap} {idea}The verse asks a simpler question: are you mindful of Allah? Then use the front door.{/idea}
old: The harder or stranger a practice looks, the more pious it is.
new: Real righteousness is taqwa, not invented outward rituals.
try: Look at the next new moon and use it to plan one act of worship for the month.

title: Even in conflict: do not transgress.
subtitle: Limits that hold when tempers do not
then: Abu Al-'Aliyah said this was the first verse about fighting revealed in Madinah, and the Prophet ﷺ {idea}fought only those who fought him.{/idea} Al-Hasan Al-Basri said transgression includes {trap}harming women, children, the elderly, worshippers in their houses of worship, and needlessly burning trees or killing animals.{/trap}
now: A fight with a sibling, an ex, a coworker. In the heat, you want to use everything: their secrets, their family, their past. {idea}The verse draws a line even in real conflict.{/idea} Do not drag in people who were never part of it, and do not go past what is fair.
old: Once someone wrongs me, I can hit back however I like.
new: Even when I am wronged, Allah's limits still bind me.
try: In your next argument, name one line you will not cross, and keep it.

title: Turning people from Allah is worse than killing.
subtitle: Measuring harm honestly, and respecting the sanctuary
then: The early Muslims had been driven from their homes in Makkah. Ibn Kathir explains that those fighting them were {trap}associating partners with Allah and blocking His path{/trap}, which the scholars called worse than killing. Yet even then, {idea}no fighting at Al-Masjid Al-Haram unless attacked there first.{/idea}
now: Think about the harms you do not count. Mocking someone's prayer until they stop. Making a younger relative ashamed of their faith. {trap}It leaves no bruise.{/trap} {idea}The verse says turning someone away from Allah is among the heaviest harms there is.{/idea}
old: Only physical harm is real harm.
new: Pushing someone away from Allah is a deep harm, even if no one sees it.
try: Encourage, instead of mocking, someone trying to come closer to Allah.

title: If they stop, Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
subtitle: The door that stays open even to enemies
then: Right after the hardest verses about fighting comes one short line: {reward}if they cease, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.{/reward} Ibn Kathir notes how at Hudaybiyyah, when news came that 'Uthman had not been killed, {idea}the Prophet ﷺ abandoned the fight and returned to peace.{/idea}
now: Your brother finally stops the silent treatment and sends a message. Part of you wants to make him pay a bit longer. {reward}The verse ends conflict with mercy, not with one more blow.{/reward} When someone stops, let it stop.
old: Once someone has hurt me, I should keep them at a distance forever.
new: When the other side stops, I make room for Allah's forgiveness and mercy.
try: Reply warmly to one person who has tried to end a quarrel with you.

title: No aggression except against the wrongdoers.
subtitle: The aim is an end to oppression, not endless war
then: The verse sets a purpose and an endpoint: until {trap}fitnah{/trap} is gone and worship is for Allah. {idea}If they cease, there is no aggression except against wrongdoers.{/idea} Abu Al-'Aliyah said the Prophet ﷺ fought only those who fought him and avoided non-combatants.
now: A dispute in the family has a clear wrong at its center. Once it is fixed, the anger often keeps spreading: to the in-laws, the kids, anyone on "their side." {idea}The verse narrows it: oppose the wrong, not everyone near it.{/idea}
old: Everyone connected to the person who wronged me is part of the problem.
new: Only wrongdoing is to be opposed, and when it stops, so do I.
try: Be kind today to someone you have treated coldly only because of who they are connected to.

title: Respond only with the like, and fear Allah.
subtitle: Justice measured, not anger unleashed
then: Ibn Kathir says the verse relates to the Prophet ﷺ being turned away from 'Umrah in a sacred month, then entering the next year. Jabir said he {idea}would not fight in the sacred months unless first attacked.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says the verse {idea}ordains justice even with the polytheists{/idea}, and then: {reward}Allah is with those who fear Him.{/reward}
now: Your colleague embarrassed you in a meeting. You plan to embarrass them twice as badly at the next one. {trap}Revenge always wants interest.{/trap} {idea}The verse caps it at the like, then turns your eyes to Allah.{/idea}
old: If someone hurts me, they should get back more than they gave.
new: Justice never goes beyond the wrong, and taqwa often asks for less.
try: Next time you want to get even, do less than the like, or nothing, for Allah.

title: Holding back your money can be your ruin.
subtitle: Spend, do not destroy yourself, and do good

row.title: ihsan
sub: Allah loves the doers of good

then: When people said a fighter was throwing himself to destruction, Abu Ayyub Al-Ansari corrected them: the verse came about the Ansar, who said {trap}let us go back to our estates and attend to them{/trap} once Islam was strong. Ibn 'Abbas said it is about {trap}refraining from spending for Allah.{/trap}
now: Your salary went up. The savings app shows a nice number. The charity request sits unread. {trap}The danger the verse names is not reckless giving; it is comfortable holding.{/trap} {reward}Allah loves those who do good beautifully.{/reward}
old: Keeping my money safe is the careful, responsible thing.
new: Holding back from good can be the real ruin. Giving is safety.
try: Set up one small regular donation today, even a tiny amount.

title: Complete it for Allah, even when the road is blocked.
subtitle: Hajj and 'Umrah, and the day they were stopped

row.title: for Allah
sub: He gave a way to finish

then: Ibn Kathir says part of this verse came in the year of Hudaybiyyah, when {trap}the Prophet ﷺ and 1400 Companions were stopped from reaching the House.{/trap} They hesitated when told to end their ihram, until they saw him ﷺ shave his head, then followed. {idea}Complete it for Allah{/idea}, even when the plan changes. The details are for scholars.
now: You saved for years to go, and the visa was refused. Or you set out to finish the Quran this year and illness stopped you. {idea}The verse is about intention held for Allah and finished in the way He allows.{/idea} When you hesitate, watch how the Prophet ﷺ acted.
old: If I cannot do it the way I planned, the effort was wasted.
new: What I begin for Allah, I finish for Allah, in the way He makes possible.
try: Pick one good thing you started and left unfinished. Do one step toward it today.

title: Pack provisions, but the best provision is taqwa.
subtitle: No foul talk, no sin, no quarrelling on the way
then: The verse sets the months of Hajj and what to leave behind once you enter it: {trap}intimacy, sin, and disputing.{/trap} Ibn Kathir notes some scholars explained fusuq through the hadith that {trap}cursing a Muslim is fusuq.{/trap} Then: {reward}whatever good you do, Allah knows it{/reward}, and the best provision is taqwa.
now: Long queues, heat, crowds, a delayed bus. Hajj or a family road trip, this is where tempers flare. {idea}You packed snacks and chargers. Did you pack patience?{/idea} The verse says the best thing you carry is mindfulness of Allah.
old: As long as I prepared well, the trip will go fine.
new: The most important thing I carry on any journey is taqwa.
try: On your next trip, decide beforehand that you will not argue, and keep it.
